### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/automation.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**32** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f60f4ea3ca7dd6b646014d02f52c2a9ae13e0820`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/automation.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `defaultValue (literal, 34 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **146** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f60f4ea3ca7dd6b646014d02f52c2a9ae13e0820` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e2023d50b6eb0b87ce7e1919b5c992cd191c19dd` — the merge of head `a2c646635bd4b3517acf61d215c1f4a78b933a69` into base `f60f4ea3ca7dd6b646014d02f52c2a9ae13e0820`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e2023d50b6eb0b87ce7e1919b5c992cd191c19dd && git checkout e2023d50b6eb0b87ce7e1919b5c992cd191c19dd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f60f4ea3ca7dd6b646014d02f52c2a9ae13e0820 a2c646635bd4b3517acf61d215c1f4a78b933a69 && git checkout -B drift-repro f60f4ea3ca7dd6b646014d02f52c2a9ae13e0820 && git merge --no-ff a2c646635bd4b3517acf61d215c1f4a78b933a69

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f60f4ea3ca7dd6b646014d02f52c2a9ae13e0820
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f60f4ea3ca7dd6b646014d02f52c2a9ae13e0820` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · contract review + ACCEPT · seat `domain:ui#1` · 2026-10-26T23:35Z

Head `a2c64663` (read from the PR object).

- **Shape.** Draft on `main`, `Fixes #26304` and `Fixes #25872`: one PR across spec, engine and console, as ruling 6422899013 and triage 6427137154 allow (the #26134 shape). 16 files, +1094/-18. Changeset: `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@object-ui/app-shell` minor. `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`. The skills and eval owed under #26184 are filed as #26347 (governed surface) and named in the body.
- **Checks pinned to the head.** All check runs completed: 0 failing, 0 pending. The seat's landing script checked this before posting.
- **Governed surface.** `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 26355`: 0 of 16 paths hit the register.
- **Contract review: PASS.**
  - **Name.** `record_link` (`SCREEN_FIELD_RECORD_LINK_TYPE`), not `record`, because `FieldType` already has `'record'` (a name-keyed sub-object map) and screen field types borrow that vocabulary. The seat accepts the name.
  - **Shape.** No new key. `type` stays `z.string().optional()`, and the rule is a branch of the existing `ScreenFieldConfigSchema` `superRefine`. A blank or absent `reference` raises the exported `…_REFERENCE_REQUIRED` message, and an absent or `null` `defaultValue` raises `…_DEFAULT_VALUE_REQUIRED`. Each of `required`, `options`, `placeholder`, `min` and `max` present with any value raises `screenFieldRecordLinkRefusedKey(key)` at its own path. The branch returns before the `lookup` rule. These are exactly ruling B's parameters.
  - **Engine.** In `screen-input-contract.ts`, any value under a `record_link` field's name (`null` included, visible or not) fails with `invalid_value` in `400 INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT`: "Screen field "NAME" shows a record and takes no value — leave it out of the resume". It is never bound, and the pause survives. The value-binding path skips the field.
  - **Console.** `ScreenView.tsx`'s `ScreenFieldInput` renders the record's display name as a link to its record page. `visibleWhen` works as usual, and an empty id renders "—".
  - **Surfaces.** `api-surface` and `export-origins` gain the new exports; the docs (`flows.mdx` plus the generated reference) and the `screen-nodes.ts` descriptor text follow.
- **Evidence (dev, report 6429522132).** New tests 9+6+2+6 and dogfood 2/2 (two created records shown and linked; a resume carrying the field's value refused). Full suites: spec 23263, automation 2707, app-shell neighbours 1794. Type-checks and the Console build exit 0. All 5 ablations go red. Gates: 114/115 exit 0; `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` was not measurable locally, and CI ran it on this head.
- **Serial constraints.** No other open PR touches these spec, engine or console files. No sdui record moves (app-shell is outside the closure). The ⛔ paths are untouched.

Landing: ready + auto-merge through the relay.
